# DeepSeek-Harness-Headroom-Plugin

Bring Headroom — a local-first
context-compression toolkit — to the **DeepSeek Harness** as a native

context-compression toolkit — to the **DeepSeek Harness** as a native plugin.

After installing, your DSH can compress large blobs on demand and retrieve the
originals byte-for-by

te, and any provider you point at the bundled proxy gets
compressed transparently — no changes to yo

compressed transparently — no changes to your prompts.
**中文文档**
## What you get
Three native tools, exposed through Headroom's own MCP server:
| Tool | What it does |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_compress` | Compress a large blob (tool output, file, log, search result)

→ compressed text + a retrieval hash |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_retrieve` | Fetch the byte-identi

cal original back by that hash |
| `mcp__headroom__headroom_stats` | Session stats: compressions, to
kens saved, estimated cost |
Two ways to use them, and they are independent:

**1. On-demand tools — works with any provider.** The model decides when to call
them. Nothing about

your traffic changes; you gain compression only when the agent
chooses to use it.

**2. Transparent compression — an HTTP proxy.** Every byte of traffic through a
repointed provider i

s compressed automatically, whether or not the model asks.
Measured on a 500-row tool result:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The FATAL row (id 67) survived compression, and the model still answered with it.
Compression is **r

eversible**: originals live in a local store and come back
byte-identical, so nothing is lost — it i

s only deferred. Byte-identity is a
property of the *store*, not of the compacted text: what the mod

el reads inline is
lossy, and the original is recovered by asking for it.
## Install
**Prerequisites:** a working DSH profile, and `uv`/`uvx` on `PATH`.

If `uvx --version` does not print a version yet, install `uv` first — it is the one
prerequisite, an
d the same command works on Windows, macOS and Linux:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Reopen the terminal afterwards and check `uvx --version`. Nothing else is
required: `uvx` fetches He

adroom and all of its Python dependencies by itself,
so there is no Python environment to create and
no package to build.

Clone this repository anywhere you like — the MCP row starts `uvx` from `PATH`, so
it does not care

where the bundle is installed; only the `install_bundle` step
needs an absolute path to locate the b

the bundle is installed; only the `install_bundle` step
needs an absolute path to locate the bundle.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Nothing needs building. Headroom itself is fetched by `uvx` on first use, and the
proxy environment
is created on demand by its launcher.
### Step 1 — nothing to configure

The shipped patch is zero-config — it pulls up the upstream `headroom mcp serve`
directly via `uvx`
on `PATH`, so there is nothing to edit:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`command` has no directory component, and the stdio transport resolves it through
the `PATH` (`cross

-spawn`), so neither the install location nor the Host's working
directory matters any more — which

is exactly what makes a config-only patch
portable. `uvx` is the same name on Windows (`uvx.exe`), m

acOS, and Linux, so the
MCP row has no `.cmd`/`.sh` platform split. `args` reaches the child as the

argv
verbatim, so `headroom-ai[mcp]` needs no quoting.
### Step 2 — install the bundle
[代码示例省略，未执行]

That runs `pnpm` in your profile, links `@local/dsh-headroom` into
`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_m

odules`, and applies the patch to the live
profile. Success reports `application: applied` with empt

y `warnings`. Restart
DSH if your profile is not the live one. Once installed, the `headroom-mcp` ro

w is
`active` and the three `mcp__headroom__*` tools are immediately usable — no need
to launch the
Harness from any particular directory.

> This one path is unavoidably absolute — `install_bundle` is told *where the
> bundle is* by you. E
verything after it is relative.
### Step 3 — remove it again
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### A note on environment variables

DSH scrubs the environment it hands to MCP children: any name matching
`/KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i

` is dropped, as is any name beginning with `DSH_`
(`dsh-subprocess/lib/index.js:32,52`). This bundl

e's variables are all named
`HEADROOM_*`, so they pass through untouched — but it is worth knowing b

efore you
add a credential-style name of your own.

`HEADROOM_DSH_WORKSPACE` overrides the launchers' workspace detection. You only
need it if you invok
e a launcher from a relocated or symlinked location.

whole chain end-to-end — the sanitizer, model discover

y, a real SSE stream, and

ich stage failed and why. `--only header` runs the offline

xit code is non-zero on failure, so it

## Transparent compression (the proxy)

Start the proxy — **nothing auto-starts it**, and it needs to be told where to

There is deliberately **no built-in upstream**. A proxy that silently forwarded to
an endpoint you d

id not choose would send your content and your API key somewhere
unexpected, so the launcher exits w

ith an error instead of guessing. Give it an
argument, `HEADROOM_UPSTREAM_URL`, or a pre-existing `O
PENAI_TARGET_API_URL`.
Then point a provider's `baseURL` at it:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The proxy forwards to `OPENAI_TARGET_API_URL` and passes the client's
`Authorization` header through

unchanged, so the provider key stays whatever DSH
already sends — nothing is duplicated, intercepte

d, or stored. Per-request token
accounting appears in the response headers (`x-headroom-tokens-befor
